display.purpose: Hero headline only. Anybody at 850 weight and 118% width, 16-18ch measure. Emphasis is a color change to Rust Glow, never an italic.

headline.purpose: Stage headings at 800 weight and 112% width, capped at 22ch. Carries the floated stage numeral.

title.purpose: Install card headings, paired with a 1rem stroke icon in Rust Glow.

body.purpose: Running prose at 62ch, hero lede at 46ch. Anybody 400.

label.purpose: Silkscreen micro-type: OS tabs, meta facts, trail numerals, alt-install headings, HUD track label.

metric.purpose: Silkscreen spec-sheet values with tabular figures; the unit after the number is Anybody in Dust.

code.purpose: Install commands, inline code, and tool tags in the system ui-monospace stack. Deliberately not a display face: a command should look like the reader's own terminal. The installer command steps to 0.75rem below 34rem.

motion.name: ease-landing
motion.purpose: The only easing curve on the page. Used for the capture-plate wipe and the mascot hop, never for an entrance wipe.

motion.name: headline-wipe
motion.value: clip-path inset(0 0 100% 0) to inset(0 0 0 0) over 760ms steps(7, jump-none)
motion.purpose: Hero headline entrance. Hard-edged, stepped, gated on prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference and the js class.

motion.name: ridge-in
motion.value: clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0) to inset(0 0 0 0) over 620ms steps(8, jump-none)
motion.purpose: The ridge draws itself left to right.

motion.name: land
motion.value: translateY(-3.5rem) to 0 with opacity, 820ms steps(4, jump-none), 120ms delay
motion.purpose: The mascot falls and lands on the ridge line.

motion.name: idle
motion.value: translateY(0 to -3px) over 3.2s steps(2, jump-none) infinite

motion.name: hop
motion.purpose: Mascot hops once after a successful copy.

motion.name: capture-rise
motion.purpose: Section capture plates wipe in on intersection. Slower than the hero so the two never read as one effect.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Every animation and transition collapses under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

breakpoints.name: phone-narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Installer stacks its copy plate under the command, filename label drops, HUD track label drops.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Command type steps up to 0.8125rem; install-card copy plate returns inline.

breakpoints.name: shell-pad
breakpoints.purpose: Shell gutter widens to 2rem; trail stops tighten their padding.

breakpoints.name: stage-pad
breakpoints.purpose: Stage padding steps to 6.5rem; hero mascot width steps to 8.5rem.

breakpoints.name: grid-two
breakpoints.purpose: Proof grid goes three-up; install pair splits into two columns; footer splits.

breakpoints.name: hud-links
breakpoints.purpose: HUD section links appear and the CTA stops claiming the auto margin.

breakpoints.name: split
breakpoints.purpose: Prose/capture splits engage, including the reversed variant.

breakpoints.name: alt-two
breakpoints.purpose: Alternative install cards go two-up; set by the longest command fitting on one line.

breakpoints.name: hero-desktop
breakpoints.purpose: Complement of 64rem: below it the stage reserves the mascot lane as bottom padding.

breakpoints.name: desktop
breakpoints.purpose: Hero takes min-height, copy caps at 46rem, mascot moves to the right edge of the ridge.

breakpoints.name: shell-max
breakpoints.purpose: Stage padding 8rem, shell gutter 2.5rem, alt installs three-up, install cards pad 1.75rem.

narrative.overview:
The page is a planet you land on and a series of stages you clear. A pixel-art mascot stands on a stepped ridge; each capability is a numbered stage on a rail below the horizon. The interface is built from the same blocks the mascot is built from: flat plates, hard edges, and a 1px seam between every surface. Nothing floats. Nothing glows. Depth comes from the ground ladder — four near-black steps — and from the seam, not from shadow.

The palette is almost entirely absence: near-black grounds, bone type, dust secondary, and one rust accent that behaves like a light source without ever becoming one. Rust marks action and position — the primary plate, the active stage flag, the underline under the current stop, the small square before each meta fact, the stage numerals. It is never used as body text. A single cool cyan exists for one job only: the focus ring.

Two type voices carry the whole system. Anybody, a variable face run wide (108–118% width) and heavy (800–850) for headlines, speaks as the product. Silkscreen, a bitmap face, prints as the machine: stage numerals, OS tabs, commands, labels, spec figures, meta facts. The division is strict — if a human wrote the sentence, it is Anybody; if a machine would print it, it is Silkscreen or monospace.
keyCharacteristics: Flat, bordered plates on a four-step near-black ground ladder; no shadow, blur, or glass anywhere.
Square corners on every surface; the only curves are in the mascot and the SVG ridge.
One rust accent, used as fill, flag, dot, and numeral — never as body text.
Stepped, hard-edged motion: clip wipes in steps() frames, not eased fades.
Body copy held to 62ch; headlines capped at 16–22ch so they break in short, blunt lines.

rules.name: The Rust Is a Verb Rule
rules.body: Rust appears as a fill, a flag, a dot, an underline, or a numeral — never as the color of a sentence. The stylesheet has no color: var(--mars); every rust-colored word is Rust Glow.

rules.name: The One Cool Note Rule
rules.body: Cyan is the focus ring and nothing else. It never becomes a link color, a hover state, a chart accent, or a decorative highlight.

rules.name: The Ground Ladder Rule
rules.body: Depth steps one rung at a time: Ground Ink → Panel Ink → Bar Ink → Plate Ink. Never skip a rung, never invent a fifth near-black, never lighten a panel to make it pop — the 1px seam does that job.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Anybody speaks; Silkscreen prints. A sentence a human wrote is never set in Silkscreen, and a machine fact (a numeral, a command, an OS name, a file name) is never set in Anybody.

rules.name: The Width Is the Emphasis Rule
rules.body: Scale and width move together. Display is 850 weight at 118% width; headline is 800 at 112%; body is 400 at normal width. There is no italic anywhere in the system, and no weight below 400.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Prose stops at 62ch, the hero lede at 46ch, headlines at 16–22ch. Nothing on the page runs full-width as text.

rules.name: The Edge, Not the Lift Rule
rules.body: State is signalled by swapping fill or color — never by raising, blurring, or glowing an element. A hover changes background and text color; it does not add a shadow, a translate, or a scale.

rules.name: The Seam Rule
rules.body: Two surfaces touch through a 1px line, never through a gap, a shadow, or a radius. Adjacent cards are separated by a 1px grid gap filled with --line, so the seam is the gap.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: Zero radius on every surface, control, and plate. A rounded corner is a different world.

rules.name: The Pixelated Rule
rules.body: Any raster of the mascot or mark is scaled with image-rendering: pixelated. Never let a pixel asset interpolate.

rules.name: The Steps Rule
rules.body: Entrances are clip wipes timed in steps() frames. No eased fades, no blur-ins, no parallax on content.

rules.name: The Working Action Rule
rules.body: The primary action is shown as the real, copyable thing — a command in a bordered plate with a copy button — not as a button that leads to one.

dos: keep every surface square and flat: 0 radius, 1px seams, and the ink ladder for depth.
use rust for action and position only — fills, flags, dots, underlines, numerals — and Rust Glow for any rust-colored word.
set machine facts (numerals, commands, OS names, file names, labels) in Silkscreen or monospace, and human sentences in Anybody.
gate every entrance on `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` and on the `js` class, so a no-JS or reduced-motion visitor sees the finished frame.
hold prose to 62ch and headlines to 16–22ch.

keep every action at least 2.75rem tall — the HUD plate and the quiet copy actions set `min-height: 2.75rem`; the primary and secondary buttons reach it through padding — and give each a visible `:focus-visible` ring in Focus Cyan.
let the mascot's feet meet the ridge line at every breakpoint; the ridge is the ground, not a decoration behind the copy.
donts: Don't add a shadow, glow, blur, or backdrop-filter. There are none in the build and the world does not have a vocabulary for them.
Don't round a corner, on any element, for any reason.
Don't use a gradient as a surface fill, a text fill, or a control fill. Gradients exist only in the page ground vignette, the 1px star field, the horizon hairline, and the trail's scroll-edge mask.
Don't set body copy in rust. Mars Rust on Ground Ink is 4.60:1 — it is a mark color, not a reading color.
Don't use Focus Cyan for anything but the focus ring.
Don't introduce a second accent hue, a warm neutral, or a brand gradient.
Don't ease an entrance. Stepped frames only.
Don't put a kicker, eyebrow, or all-caps label above a headline — the stage numeral inside the heading is the only heading marker this world uses.
